title: The BMC decides whether a request came from the host or the network by reading a header
index_line: T-0048 · AUTH_DECISION · `X-Server-Addr`/`Host` classification stands in for network position on a Redfish interface · c/any-BMC · corroborated
invariant_violated: A management controller has two very different callers — the host it sits in, and the operator on the network — and it tells them apart by looking at the request. Network position is the only signal it cannot be lied to about, and it is the one signal the code does not use: it prefers a header the caller writes.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated attacker sends a management request with `X-Server-Addr` or `Host` set to describe the host itself
the interface parses the header and classifies the request as originating from the host side
host-side requests are treated as already trusted, so no session or credential is required
the Redfish operations proceed against the controller as an authenticated administrator
the attacker reaches firmware write / reset / shell surfaces the controller exposes to its local host

source.http.header.value: `X-Server-Addr`, `Host`, `X-Forwarded-*` — a header that a *proxy or host* is expected to set and a client can also set

header.forwarding.value: the trust boundary for forwarding headers: which ones the front end overwrites and which it passes through

guard.none.value: no check that the request actually arrived on the internal interface (source address, mTLS, per-interface listener)

sink.exec.shell.value: the privileged controller surface reached after the classification passes

preconditions.expr: the management interface is reachable from an untrusted network path
the authentication decision consults a request header for host/peer classification
the header is accepted from the client rather than overwritten by a front end

check.spec: send two requests that differ only in the header value and compare the authorization verdicts

success: a Redfish request with a spoofed host header returns data or performs an action that requires authentication
the same request without the header is refused — the header is the switch
the effect needs no credentials at all
failure_like: the interface classifies the caller by its actual source address or a TLS client identity
a front end overwrites the header before the service sees it
false_positive: a 401 on the Redfish root — that is the interface working
a public read-only Redfish resource answering without auth (some are unauthenticated by design)

hazards: this is the header-trust class applied to *network position*: any 'are you internal?' check that reads a header is the same bug
BMCs sit outside the OS and often outside the EDR — compromise here is host-level and persistent, which is why the impact is not 'an API'
inventory the listeners: the same controller frequently exposes the interface on more than one network, and only one of them is meant to be internal
distinct from T-0045 (path normalization) and T-0046 (missing check): here the check exists and is fooled
non_transfers: interfaces that bind the internal-facing service to a separate listener or require mTLS from the host agent
proxies that always overwrite forwarding headers
